decisions.reason: It remained listed through 2024 and supports the firm's fast-response service promise, but its limited prominence and overlap with other express offers make it a plausible candidate for consolidation if results stay below aspiration.

The 72-hour program is close to the core offer and differentiates on delivery speed, so a large firm with service slack is likely to retain it unless its high execution costs cause a clear performance shortfall.
A dedicated page in both years suggests results at or above aspiration for this broader express line, making continuation the more likely choice.
The digital ordering platform fits the firm's strategic move toward deeper advisory and service support and likely benefits from organisational slack while usage scales.
Its upgrade from a mention to a dedicated page in 2024 signals improving acceptance in a regulation-sensitive core segment, so management would likely keep it.
